text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — Detecting sustained 5xx surge for customer 'Sierra' served from dedicated pool dp-west-3. Aggregate 5xx ~72% over last 3m, median p50 latency 1.2s -> 3.4s. Suspected KV prefix cache thrash / eviction storms causing hot-tenant amplification. Paging oncall.

sara (oncall): I'm on it. Pulling kv cache metrics now. Can someone grab recent deploys for dp-west-3?

mike (eng-sre): I have the pool deploys — nothing unusual in CI. Attaching quick checks: prefix hit-rate for tenant=sierra dropped from 98% -> 9% over the last 10m. Errors align with cache lookup timeouts and OOM spikes in the per-tenant store.

jen (eng-ml): Sounds like prefix cache pollution. Sierra has a very spiky keyspace pattern (many unique prefixes per request) and we saw a ramp in customer-side batch size yesterday. That can blow up prefix index memory and trigger eviction thrash.

sara (oncall): Confirmed. Impact: customer traffic to dp-west-3 only. No other customers on pool show the same severity. ETA for mitigation ideas?

mike (eng-sre): Immediate options (ordered by risk/impact):
  1) Disable prefix caching for tenant 'sierra' (fast, per-tenant flag). This avoids thrash but increases token compute cost.
  2) Apply per-tenant prefix-cache entry cap + LRU safeguard (safer, may take few mins to propagate to edge nodes).
  3) Evict suspect prefixes and bump cache TTLs for system prefixes only.
  4) Route Sierra traffic to fallback pool (dp-fallback) — higher cost but isolates.

lia (eng-platform): I can push a per-tenant toggle through the control plane — it's a fast config patch: `{"tenant": "sierra", "prefix_cache_enabled": false}`. Will require a rolling config push to dp-west-3 nodes.

sara (oncall): Let's do (1) now to stop the immediate harm, then (2) as follow-up. mike, jen, can you coordinate validation? lia, please prepare the toggle.

lia (eng-platform): Preparing rollout. Will send the config via the control plane. Deploy-bot will record activities.

deploy-bot: Config change queued: toggle_prefix_cache OFF for tenant=sierra on pool=dp-west-3 by lia. JobID=cfg-20260315-004

mike (eng-sre): Checking for edge artifacts. Running quick grep on node logs for prefix eviction messages.

jen (eng-ml): Also checking model runtime logs — if cache misses spike, expect higher compute. We should enable short-term autoscale buffer on dp-west-3 to avoid 503s while cache disabled.

sara (oncall): Lia, can we do both: toggle + increase pool buffer by 20% for 10m?

lia (eng-platform): Yep. Pushing both now.

deploy-bot: Job cfg-20260315-004 started. Rolling to 6/6 nodes in dp-west-3. Estimated 1m per node.

nate (customer-success): Drafting message to Sierra.

nate (customer-success): "We detected elevated errors impacting your service. We're applying a configuration to disable prefix caching for your tenant to immediately mitigate the issue; this may increase compute cost temporarily. Expect partial recovery within ~10 minutes. We'll follow up with root cause and longer-term fix." LMK if edits.

sara (oncall): Good. Keep it conservative.

mike (eng-sre): Logs show the first node patch succeeded. After first two nodes patched, 5xx dropped to ~28% for shard subset.

jen (eng-ml): After cache off, prefix hit-rate is irrelevant but overall latency is stabilizing. CPU usage on dp-west-3 is up 18% as expected.

lia (eng-platform): Config rollout complete on all nodes. Job cfg-20260315-004 succeeded. AuditID=audit-7801

deploy-bot: cfg-20260315-004 success. Noting increased autoscale buffer: pool dp-west-3 capacity +20% for 10m.

sara (oncall): Monitoring. 5xx now at ~6% and dropping. Latency back to ~1.1s median. Marking customer impact reduced.

nate (customer-success): Sent message to Sierra (support channel). They acknowledged and appreciate quick update. They asked if this will affect cost — I warned about temporary compute increase.

mike (eng-sre): For follow-up, propose these next steps:
  - Roll in per-tenant prefix-entry cap and LRU (config change) to prevent recurrence.
  - Add alert for sudden prefix cardinality growth per tenant (early detection).
  - Add a rapid routing playbook to move tenant traffic to fallback pool if cache disabled.
  - Quantify cost delta for Sierra and offer credit if material.

jen (eng-ml): Also, we should analyze recent customer-side request patterns. There was a sudden spike in unique prefixes from one of their services — might be a client-side regression.

lia (eng-platform): I'll schedule a follow-up PR to add the per-tenant cap. Can we get an ops window for validation tomorrow?

sara (oncall): I'll prepare an incident page and schedule a postmortem. Can someone save the node logs and snapshot the prefix cache metrics? mike, jen?

mike (eng-sre): Saved logs to gs://redwood-incidents/1818002222/sierra-logs.tar.gz. Also exported cache metrics. path: `gs://redwood-metrics/incident-1818002222/prefix-metrics.csv`

jen (eng-ml): Saved model runtime traces to the same bucket.

nate (customer-success): Sierra asked for an ETA on when caching will be re-enabled.

sara (oncall): We'll only re-enable when we've validated the cap/LRU in a canary with their traffic pattern. Tentative: after per-tenant cap rollout and 24h observation. Tell them we'll follow up with exact timeline in the postmortem.

lia (eng-platform): Note: disabling prefix cache increases egress compute billing. Ops-tagging incident to billing review.

deploy-bot: Autoscale buffer expired after 10m; pool dp-west-3 capacity returned to baseline.

sara (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. We'll keep this thread open for postmortem notes. Great cross-team work. :thumbsup:

mike (eng-sre): Filing postmortem with recommended actions and timeline.

jen (eng-ml): Quick note for the PMs: consider adding rate-limit guidance for customer-side batching/unique-prefix generation.

nate (customer-success): Customer Sierra appreciated the fast mitigation. They requested the postmortem and any client-side recommendations.

ops-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED — 5xx rate reduced to <1% for tenant 'Sierra' on dp-west-3. Active mitigations: prefix_cache disabled (tenant override). Follow-up: per-tenant cap rollout (P0), prefix cardinality alert (P1). Incident closed but ticketing follow-up required.

sara (oncall): Handoff to daytime oncall (mike) at next rotation for postmortem ownership.

mike (eng-sre): Acknowledged. I'll own the postmortem and follow-ups.

sara (oncall): Thanks all. I'll update the incident tracker and schedule the RCA meeting for 2026-03-16 16:00 UTC.

nate (customer-success): Noted. I'll attach customer communication and billing note to the ticket.

-- end of thread --
